1891:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this section, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Blighted property, blighted, or blight means any urbanized or developed property which:
(1) Presents two or more of the following criteria:
a. Uninhabitable, unsafe, or abandoned structure as determined by the public officer or his or her designee;
b. Inadequate provisions for ventilation, light, air, or sanitation as determined by the public officer or his or her designee;
c. An imminent harm to life or other property caused by fire, flood, hurricane, tornado, earthquake, storm, or other natural catastrophe respecting which the governor has declared a state of emergency under the state law or has certified the need for disaster assistance under federal law; provided, however, this division shall not apply to property unless the relevant public agency has given notice in writing to the property owner regarding specific harm caused by the property and the owner has failed to take reasonable measures to remedy the harm;
d. A site identified by the Federal Environmental Protection Agency as a superfund site pursuant to 42 U.S.C. Section 9601, et seq., or having environmental contamination to an extent that requires remedial investigation or a feasibility study;
e. Repeated illegal activity on the individual property of which the property owner knew or should have known; or
f. The maintenance of the property is below state or county codes for at least one year after written notice of the code violation to its owner.
(2) Is conducive to ill health, transmission of disease, infant mortality, or crime in the immediate proximity of the property.
Property shall not be deemed blighted solely because of aesthetic conditions.
Building inspector means a certified inspector possessing the requisite qualifications to determine minimal code compliance.
Community redevelopment means any activity, project, or service necessary or incidental to achieving the redevelopment or revitalization of a redevelopment area or portion thereof designated for redevelopment through an urban redevelopment plan or through local ordinances relating to the repair, closing, and demolition of buildings and structures unfit for human habitation.
Governing authority means the board of commissioners of Clayton County, Georgia.
Millage or millage rate means the levy, in mills, which is established by the governing authority for purposes of financing, in whole or in part, the levying jurisdiction's general fund expenses for the fiscal year.
Person means such individual(s), partnership, corporations, business entities and associations which return real property for ad valorem taxation or who are chargeable by law for the taxes on the property.
Public officer means the Clayton County Director of Community Development, the warden, the chief of police or such officer or employee of the county as designated by the director of community development, warden or chief of police to perform the duties and responsibilities hereafter set forth in this article.
(Ord. No. 2024-253, § 1, 11-5-24)

1893:
(a) In order for a parcel of real property to be officially designated as maintained in a blighted condition and subject to increased taxation, the following steps must be completed:
(1) An inspection must be performed on the parcel of property. In order for an inspection to be performed,
a. A request may be made by the public officer or by at least five residents of the county in writing for inspection of a parcel of property, said inspection to be based on the criteria as delineated in ordinance, or
b. The public officer may cause a survey of existing housing conditions to be performed, or may refer to any such survey conducted or finalized within the previous five years, to locate or identify any parcels which may be in a blighted condition and for which a full inspection should be conducted to determine if that parcel of property meets the criteria set out in this section for designation as being maintained in a blighted condition.
(2) A written inspection report of the findings for any parcel of property inspected pursuant to subsection (1) above shall be prepared and submitted to the public officer. Where feasible, photographs of the conditions found to exist on the property on the date of inspection shall be made and included in the inspection report. Where compliance with minimum construction, housing, occupancy, fire and life safety codes in effect within the county are in question, the inspection shall be conducted by a certified inspector possessing the requisite qualifications to determine minimal code compliance.
(3) Following completion of the inspection report, the public officer shall make a determination, in writing, that a property in question is a blighted property. The public officer shall cause a written notice of his determination that the real property at issue is being maintained in a blighted condition to be mailed via first class mail and e-mailed, if known, to the person(s) shown on the most recent tax digest of Clayton County as responsible for payment of ad valorem taxes assessed thereon; provided, however, where through the existence of reasonable diligence it becomes known to the public officer that real property has been sold or conveyed since publication of the most recent tax digest, written notice shall also be given to the person(s) known or reasonably believed to then own the property or be chargeable with the payment of ad valorem taxes thereon, at the best address available.
(4) The property owner may contact the public official to voluntarily remediate the conditions on the property within 30 days of receiving the written notice. Such a plan shall meet the criteria set forth in section 90-104. If no contact is initiated with the public official or if the proposed remediation is not sufficient to remove the blighted condition, then a complaint in rem shall be prepared and filed by the county attorney's office to the magistrate court of the county.
(5) The complaint shall state the two or more criteria which constitutes the blighted condition that exists on the property and what steps shall be taken to remediate the property. Service in the manner set forth at O.C.G.A. § 41-2-12 shall constitute sufficient notice to the property owner or person chargeable with the payment of ad valorem taxes for the purpose of this section, except that posting of the notice on the property will not be required.
(6) The magistrate court of the county shall issue a summons notifying interested parties that a hearing will be held before the magistrate court of the county at a date and time certain. (a) Words and phrases used in this article shall have the following meanings, unless otherwise specified:
All-terrain vehicle means any motorized vehicle designed for off-road use which is equipped with three or more low-pressure tires and with a seat to be straddled by the operator and with handlebars for steering control.
Bicycle means every device propelled by human power upon which any person may ride, having only two wheels which are in tandem and either of which is more than 13 inches in diameter.
Electric bicycle means a device with two or three wheels which has a saddle and fully operative pedals for human propulsion and also has an electric motor. For such a device to be considered an electric-assisted bicycle, it shall meet the requirements of the federal motor vehicle safety standards, as set forth in 49 CFR 571 et seq., and shall operate in such a manner that the electric motor disengages or ceases to function when the brakes are applied. The electric motor in an electric assisted bicycle shall:
(1) Have a power output of not more than 1,000 watts;
(2) Be incapable of propelling the device at a speed of more than 20 miles per hour on level ground; and
(3) Be incapable of further increasing the speed of the device when human power alone is used to propel the device at or more than 20 miles per hour.
Electric personal assistive mobility device or EPAMD means a self-balancing, two non-tandem-wheeled device designed to transport only one person and having an electric propulsion system with average power of 750 watts (one horsepower) and a maximum speed of less than 20 miles per hour on a paved level surface when powered solely by such propulsion system and ridden by an operator who weighs not more than 170 pounds.
Low-speed motor vehicle or LSMV means any four-wheeled electric vehicle whose top speed attainable in one mile is greater than 20 miles per hour but not greater than 25 miles per hour on a paved level surface and which is manufactured in compliance with those federal motor vehicle safety standards for low-speed vehicles set forth in 49 CFR 571.500 and in effect on January 1, 2001.
Moped means a motor-driven cycle equipped with two or three wheels, with or without foot pedals to permit muscular propulsion, and an independent power source providing a maximum of two brake horsepower. If a combustion engine is used, the maximum piston or rotor displacement shall be 3.05 cubic inches (50 centimeters) regardless of the number of chambers in such power source. The power source shall be capable of propelling the vehicle, unassisted, at a speed not to exceed 30 miles per hour (48.28 kilometers per hour) on level road surface and shall be equipped with a power drive system that functions directly or automatically only, not requiring clutching or shifting by the operator after the drive system is engaged.
Motorcycle means every motor vehicle having a seat or saddle for the use of the rider and designed to travel on not more than three wheels in contact with the ground, but excluding a tractor, all-terrain vehicle, dirt bike, and moped.
Motor-driven cycle means every motorcycle, including every motor scooter, with a motor which produces not to exceed five brake horsepower, every bicycle with a motor attached, and every moped.
Motorized cart means every motor vehicle having no less than three wheels and an unladen weight of 1,300 pounds or less and which cannot operate at more than 20 miles per hour.
Motorized play vehicle means a coaster, scooter, pocket bike, any other alternatively fueled device, or other motorized vehicle that is self-propelled by a motor engine, gas or electric, and is not otherwise defined in this Code as a "motorized cart," "low speed motor vehicle (SLAV)," "motor vehicle," "motorcycle," "electric bicycle," motorized skateboard," "electric personal assistive mobility device," or "motorized wheelchair."
Motorized skateboard means a self-propelled device, including Segways, that has a motor, gas or electric, a deck upon which a person may ride, not equipped with a seat, and at least two tandem wheels in contact with the ground and which is not otherwise defined in this Code as a motor vehicle," "motorcycle," "motorized play vehicle," "motor scooter," "electric personal assistive mobility device" or "motorized wheelchair."
Motorized wheelchair means a self-propelled wheelchair that is used by a physically disabled person for mobility.
Pocket motorcycle or pocket bike means a two-wheeled vehicle other than a motor vehicle, bicycle with helper motor or a motorized scooter, and which is propelled by an internal combustion engine, electric motor or other mechanical means, is capable of carrying a rider and/or passenger at a speed in excess of 20 miles per hour, and is designed to replicate the general appearance of a motorcycle, regardless of the scale of the replication.
(Ord. No. 2019-32, § II, 3-19-19)

85thpercentile speed is an index of traffic speeds for a road segment used for traffic analysis purposes. The 85 th percentile speed is the speed at which 85 percent of the vehicles are driving at or below. Historical research initiatives and studies have identified that the majority of motorists choose reasonable speeds for given road conditions; the 85 th percentile speed is the value of where most reasonable motorists operate their vehicles in a manner they perceive to be safe.
AASHTO means the American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials.
Affected area means a geographic portion of a neighborhood consisting of all property owners whose quality of life as a resident in the neighborhood, and not necessarily as a traveler through the neighborhood, is being directly impacted by the cut-through or speeding traffic problem being addressed. The affected area will include all parcels from which residents must traverse the traffic calming measure. The affected area will also include all parcels from which residents may have an alternate route without traffic calming measures, but whose lots have driveways that access the residential street for which traffic calming measures are sought.
Average daily traffic (ADT) is a unit of measure used by transportation professionals for traffic volume analysis, in units of vehicles per day (VPD). ADT for the purpose of this ordinance refers to the traffic in both directions on a particular street within a 24-hour period.

Department means the Clayton County Department of Transportation and Development.

FHWA means the Federal Highway Administration.
GDOT means the Georgia Department of Transportation.
HOA means homeowners association and property owners association.
Initiator is a real property owner who has requested an initial interest petition form and/or has assumed a primary role in circulating the initial interest petition and the subsequent traffic calming petition and undertakes to serve as the county's sole contact with respect to the progress of the initial interest petition and any subsequent traffic study and traffic calming petition.
ITE means the Institute of Transportation Engineers.
MUTCD means the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices.
Program manual means the Clayton County Traffic Calming Program Manual.
Real property owners means homeowners or other real property owners as indicated in the tax records maintained by the county's tax commissioner and board of tax assessors.
Street functional classification system means grouping of streets by the character of service they provide whether uninterrupted high-speed flow, moderate speed distributor facilities bringing motorists nearer to their destination or local access roads that provide direct access to individual residences and other destinations. Road purpose and hierarchy is determined by the purpose of the road, the traffic volume experienced and the speed of travel, while providing a balance between mobility and access. For the purpose of this article, the terms street and road are used interchangeably. Various classifications of streets shall be defined as follows:
(1) Interstate highway. Any roadway that operates at a high service level, consists of limited access, is divided, carries region-wide traffic and is generally classified as part of the interstate system.
(2) Arterial road. A street with traffic signals at important intersections and stop signs on the side streets and that carries a significant amount of trips entering and leaving an urban area typically connecting business and commercial areas to residential areas with moderate traffic volumes and vehicle speed. Street and driveway locations are typically limited to preserve mobility and safety and limit the number of direct access points.
(3) Collector road. A street designed to facilitate the collection of traffic from local streets and to provide circulation within neighborhood areas and convenient ways to reach arterial streets. Collector streets typically provide a balance between individual parcel access and mobility.
(4) Local residential street. A street designed for direct access to abutting property and to discourage through traffic. Local streets are low speed, low traffic volume streets with limited mobility.
(5) Private street. Vehicular streets and driveways which are wholly within private property, except where they intersect with other streets within public rights-of-way and are maintained by the owner(s), and a road/street that has not been accepted by the county or other governmental entity.
Traffic calming measures means those methods and processes, prescribed by AASHTO, ITE, or other nationally recognized organizations, that the county may use to reduce aggressive driving behavior that impairs the quality of life of its citizens in any neighborhood. Such measures include, but are not limited to, speed humps, speed tables, traffic circles, median islands, chicanes, lateral shifts, chokers, and closures.
Traffic engineering is a branch of civil engineering that concentrates on the application of engineering principles to ensure safe and efficient operation of roads, streets, and highways for all users through sound planning, geometric design, traffic operations, and system management.
Traffic study means the process by which data pertinent to the flow, rate of speed and density of traffic, collected over a defined period of time, is measured and analyzed to determine its impact on the safety of citizens within a neighborhood or affected area.
(Ord. No. 2025-250, § 1, 11-18-25)
1955:
The board of commissioners hereby declares that it shall promote the health, safety and general public welfare of the citizens of the county by providing for the implementation of traffic calming in the public rights-of-way of the county to aid in the moderation of vehicle speed throughout the county. Generally, traffic calming is the combination of mainly physical measures that reduce the negative effects of motor vehicle use, alter driver behavior, and improve conditions for non-motorized street users. To that end, therefore, this article is adopted in order to effect the creation of traffic calming districts and to provide for the implementation of traffic calming in the public rights-of-way of the county. This article shall not be deemed to apply to property in the county other than in the public rights-of-way.
(Ord. No. 2025-250, § 1, 11-18-25)
1956:
Local residential streets with:
(a) Speed limits of 30 miles per hour or less;
(b) A documented 85 th percentile speed of more than ten miles above the posted speed limit;
(c) A traffic volume greater than 500 vehicles per day; and
(d) Grades of eight percent or less are eligible for installation of traffic calming measures.
Arterial, collector and private streets are not eligible for traffic calming measures. Cul-de-sac streets greater than 500 feet in length may be eligible for installation of traffic calming, provided they meet the other requirements of the program. Eligibility by itself does not automatically guarantee traffic calming measures are appropriate or would be recommended to and ultimately approved by the county's governing authority.
(Ord. No. 2025-250, § 1, 11-18-25)
1957:
In keeping with the general recommendation of the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices, uniformity aids in the recognition and understanding of traffic control devices. Adherence to standards and guidelines will help ensure that any given traffic calming application will be equally recognizable and require the same action on the part of the motorists regardless of where it is encountered. The design and installation of all traffic calming measures shall follow the latest research, current industry standards, and best practices as set forth by industry organizations including ITE, AASHTO, and FHWA. Engineering judgement shall be exercised in the application of traffic calming measures to ensure safe road conditions for all users.
(Ord. No. 2025-250, § 1, 11-18-25)
1958:
(a) Any person(s) interested in pursuing the installation of traffic calming measures on a local residential street, upon request to the department, will be provided with an initial interest petition of a form promulgated by the department director or designee. The person provided the petition will be identified as the Initiator for the process.
(b) The initial interest petition must be marked with the date on which it is required to be returned to the department, hereinafter referred to as the return date. Such return date shall be 60 days after the date the department issues the initial interest petition. The initial interest petition will allow for eligible petitioners to sign in favor of requesting a traffic study or to register their opposition to the traffic study and the potential installation of traffic calming measures. The initial interest petition shall include language describing the partnership between the county and the eligible petitioners, including the requirement of applicable capital up-front funding and reoccurring yearly fees in compliance with the fee structure section of this ordinance.
(c) The completed initial interest petition shall be filed with the department by the return date as provided or it shall be deemed abandoned and any further action by the county will require a new initial interest petition.
(d) In order to be considered complete, the initial interest petition shall include all the following:
(1) The full printed name, signature, home address, and daytime phone number of each person that signed the initial interest petition.
(2) The date upon which each person signed the initial interest petition.
(3) A description of the precise area for which the traffic study is requested by reference to the name of the subdivision or popular name of the neighborhood, or the streets, roads, or where appropriate the residential address number that identify the area where a perceived speeding or cut-through problem exists.
(4) The full printed name, address and daytime phone number of the initiator.
(e) Only one eligible petitioner for each residential parcel may sign the initial interest petition.
(f) The department will not consider an initial interest petition unless it is complete, per the requirements of this section, and unless at least 20 percent of the eligible petitioners in the requested area are in favor of the traffic study.
(g) A registered HOA in good standing with the Georgia Secretary of States's office can submit a resolution approved by the HOA governing body on behalf of the subdivision or requested area. The acceptance of this resolution will satisfy the 20 percent requirement.
(Ord. No. 2025-250, § 1, 11-18-25)
1959:
(a) Upon receipt of a completed initial interest petition, the department will utilize current tax records to make a determination as to whether at least 20 percent of the eligible petitioners in the requested area are in favor of the traffic study. The percentage will be calculated based on individual parcels where eligible petitioners sign affirmatively, divided by the total number of parcels in the requested area.
(b) After the department has received the complete initial interest petition, no signature will be withdrawn from an initial interest petition unless the department is notified in writing within 30 days that there is reasonable proof that fraud or other impropriety occurred regarding the obtaining of the petitioner's signature.
(c) The initiator of the initial interest petition will be notified in writing by the department as to whether the initial interest petition meets the criteria for a traffic study.
(d) In the event that the initiator moves away or is otherwise no longer the point of contact for the department and a new initiator's name and address has not been provided to the department, the department shall consider the initial interest petition abandoned and shall cease all work on processing of the initial interest petition and any subsequent traffic study.
(Ord. No. 2025-250, § 1, 11-18-25)
1960:
(a) The department will conduct traffic studies generally based on the order of complete initial interest petitions are received. The department reserves the right to change the order in which a traffic study is conducted where the department determines that there is an initial interest petition further down the pending list for an area that may relate to, or be affected by, another traffic study to be conducted on a neighboring street or area.
(b) Where a traffic study is warranted, it will be conducted at a time determined by, and within the sole discretion of the department.
(c) Upon completion of the traffic study, the department shall make a determination as to whether the results clearly demonstrate that the installation of traffic calming measures are warranted based upon the criteria established in this ordinance and the traffic calming program manual. If the department determines traffic calming measures are not warranted, the initiator of the initial interest petition shall be notified of the results in writing by the department.
(Ord. No. 2025-250, § 1, 11-18-25)
1961:
(a) Where traffic calming measures are warranted the department shall, within a reasonable time following the completion of the traffic study, prepare a traffic calming conceptual design and notify the initiator in writing.
(b) The traffic calming conceptual plan must identify the affected area and include a recommendation for a specific traffic calming measure or a combination of such measures that the department has determined to provide the most effective solution to the neighborhood's concerns. Recommendations shall take into consideration various characteristics of the individual area including pavement width, horizontal and vertical geometric elements, drainage, the location of existing traffic control items, driveway locations, and other physical features present in the area. Projected costs, applicable to both the county and the community, shall be considered in the selection of traffic calming measures keeping in mind the cost sharing fee structure identified in this ordinance.
(c) Upon completion of the conceptual plan, it shall be presented to the neighborhood at a community meeting or by another acceptable means. The public has the opportunity to ask questions, comment on the conceptual plan, provide their recommendations and suggestions for alternative plan elements. It is envisioned that this community process will be a collaborative effort between the department and the community to refine the conceptual plan, balancing the community's desires, funding availability, engineering principles, and practical applications. The department shall also seek input from the county's various public safety departments, ensuring their suggestions are considered in the process. In the event a conflict arises in the conceptual plan that cannot be successfully mitigated to the desires of the eligible petitioners, the department shall have the final decision authority over the conflict after applying sound engineering principles and judgement.
(Ord. No. 2025-250, § 1, 11-18-25)
1962:
(a) Once the conceptual plan is finalized by the department, it shall be considered the traffic calming plan for the requested area. Before the traffic calming petition is released to the initiator, the department shall identify the appropriate boundaries for a traffic calming district taking into consideration the affected area, traffic patterns, street intersections, and other related factors. Each traffic calming district shall include the tax parcel number of each lot within the said traffic calming district. The department shall estimate the cost sharing values based upon the fee structure identified in this ordinance. The department reserves the right to utilize various means to determine the cost including on-demand contracted services, internal county forces, and other methods. At the discretion of the department, the traffic calming plan could be individually bid for construction through the county's standard request for construction bids process.
(b) After the traffic calming district is determined, the traffic calming petition shall be provided to the initiator for community consideration. The initiator is responsible for circulating the traffic calming petition to all eligible petitioners in the identified district. The department can provide limited assistance to the initiator in identifying contact information for out-of-town eligible petitioners; however, it is the initiator's responsibility to contact each petitioner. In addition to the estimated cost sharing requirements, the petition shall include a statement concerning the potential impact the installation of traffic calming measures could have on public safety response times. It is understood that any eligible petitioner who signs the petition in favor of traffic calming measures acknowledges the potential impact to public safety and accepts the matter as a trade-off for the moderation of vehicle speed. The petition shall also acknowledge other generally considered negative by-products of traffic calming measures including the potential for increased vehicle noise, the diverting of traffic to adjacent streets, and the increase in street signage requirements.
(c) The traffic calming petition must be marked with the date on which it is required to be returned to the department, hereinafter referred to as the return date. Such return date shall be 60 days after the date the department issues the traffic calming petition. The traffic calming petition will allow for eligible petitioners to sign in favor of the traffic calming plan or to register their opposition to the installation of traffic calming measures.
(d) The completed traffic calming petition shall be filed with the department by the return date as provided or it shall be deemed abandoned and any further action by the county will require a new traffic calming petition and, in some situations, a new initial interest petition.
(e) In order to be considered complete, the traffic calming petition shall include the following:
(1) The full printed name, signature, home address, and daytime phone number of each person that signed the traffic calming petition.
(2) The date upon which each person signed the traffic calming petition.
(3) The full printed name, address and daytime phone number of the initiator.
(f) Only one eligible petitioner for each residential parcel may sign the traffic calming petition.
(g) The department will not consider the traffic calming petition unless it is complete, per the requirements of this section. Eligible petitioners who affirmatively signed the initial interest petition but not the traffic calming petition, will not be counted as an affirmative response for the traffic calming petition, as the traffic calming petition is a separate stand-alone petition. In order to be eligible for approval consideration by the board of commissioners, at least 55 percent of the eligible petitioners in the traffic calming district must be in favor of the traffic calming plan.
(h) The traffic calming petition requires the signature of individual real property owners as eligible petitioners. A registered HOA in good standing with the Georgia Secretary of State's office, can assist the initiator with the facilitation of the traffic calming petition, however the HOA is not authorized to represent and execute on behalf of individual real property owners. If individual parcels within the traffic calming district are owned by the HOA, then the HOA has authority to execute the petition for those parcels.
(Ord. No. 2025-250, § 1, 11-18-25)
1963:
(a) Upon receipt of a completed traffic calming petition, the department will utilize current tax records to make a determination as to whether at least 55 percent of the eligible petitioners in the traffic calming district are in favor of the traffic calming plan. The percentage will be calculated based on individual parcels where eligible petitioners sign affirmatively, divided by the total number of parcels in the traffic calming district.
(b) After the department has received the complete traffic calming petition, no signature will be withdrawn from the traffic calming petition unless the department is notified in writing within 30 days, that there is reasonable proof that fraud or other impropriety occurred regarding the obtaining of the petitioner's signature.
(c) The initiator of the traffic calming petition will be notified in writing by the department as to whether the traffic calming petition meets the criteria for approval consideration by the board of commissioners.
(d) In the event that the initiator moves away or is otherwise no longer the point of contact for the department and a new initiator's name and address has not been provided to the department, the department shall consider the traffic calming petition abandoned and shall cease all work on processing of the traffic calming petition.
(Ord. No. 2025-250, § 1, 11-18-25)
1964:
(a) If a completed traffic calming petition is confirmed to have at least 55 percent of the eligible petitioners in favor of the traffic calming plan, the petition, the traffic calming plan and supporting information shall be presented to the board of commissioners for their approval consideration at a regular or special called meeting. The board of commissioners may vote to accept or reject the traffic calming petition and plan.
(b) Should the board of commissioners approve the traffic calming petition and plan, a traffic calming tax district shall be created to include all the parcels identified in the traffic calming district. All parcels in the traffic calming district shall be responsible for funding the cost sharing portion of the capital installation costs of the traffic calming measures as identified in the traffic calming petition and in compliance with the fee structure section of this ordinance. The initiator of the traffic calming petition shall be responsible for coordinating fee collection from the eligible parcels. When a minimum of 75 percent of the cost sharing value has been collected from the eligible petitioners from the newly created traffic calming district, the construction of the traffic calming measures shall be authorized.
(c) In addition to the cost sharing portion of the capital installation costs, an annual maintenance fee in compliance with the fee structure section of this ordinance, shall be assessed to and collected from each parcel included in the traffic calming tax district. This annual maintenance fee shall be collected as part of the annual property tax assessment by the county's tax commissioner.
(Ord. No. 2025-250, § 1, 11-18-25)
1965:
(a) Upon presentation of a petition from eligible petitioners representing 75 percent of the properties in the traffic calming district, traffic calming measures previously installed may be removed. No such petition shall be presented earlier than 12 months after initial installation of the traffic calming measures.
(b) A removal petition may be obtained from the department director or the director's designee. An estimate of the costs of removal of the traffic calming measures shall be provided by the department.
(c) The removal petition shall be returned and filed with the department within 90 days of the date on which it was provided pursuant to a request, or it shall be deemed abandoned and any further action by the county shall require a new removal petition. Said petition shall indicate the property owners' agreement to pay all costs, including, but not limited to, labor, equipment, disposal of materials, notification to property owners, advertisement costs, and any other costs associated with the removal of the traffic calming measures.
(d) Upon confirmation by the department that the removal petition satisfies the conditions of this section, the removal petition shall be presented to the board of commissioners for their consideration and approval at a regular or special called meeting.
(e) Should the board of commissioners approve the removal petition, the initiator of the removal petition shall be responsible for coordinating fee collection from the traffic calming district.
(f) Upon receipt of 75 percent of the costs of removal as previously identified by the department in the removal petition, the department shall remove the traffic calming measures.
(Ord. No. 2025-250, § 1, 11-18-25)
1966:
If any provision of this article is in conflict with any state or federal law, or with any rule, regulation or order of any agency of this state or federal agency having jurisdiction of the subject matter of this article, the state or federal law or rule, regulation or order shall prevail over the conflicting section of this article.
(Ord. No. 2025-250, § 1, 11-18-25)
1967:
The board of commissioners is authorized to adopt a fee structure for traffic calming measures, which structure may be amended or modified upon properly adopted motion of the board of commissioners. The fee structure shall consist of two fees:
(a) Cost sharing of the capital installation costs. The funding of the capital installation costs shall be a partnership between the county and the approved traffic calming district. As determined by the department, the county shall fund 70 percent of the installation cost of the traffic calming plan with the eligible petitioners of the traffic calming district funding the remaining 30 percent. The initiator of the traffic calming petition shall be responsible for coordinating the fee collection from the traffic calming district.
(b) Annual maintenance fee. The board of commissioners shall establish an annual maintenance fee to be assessed per parcel in the traffic calming district. This fee shall be assessed by the tax assessor and collected as part of the annual property assessment by the county's tax commissioner.
(Ord. No. 2025-250, § 1, 11-18-25)
1968:
(a) Residential speed control is something that should be considered during the planning stages of a residential development. Prior to development of a subdivision, the developer shall consider including traffic calming measures in the preliminary plans. The implementation of traffic calming measures in the planning stage is a proactive measure to help maintain safe speeds within residential areas before they become an issue. The department is authorized to recommend specific traffic calming measures in the development process. If the development fails to adequately incorporate traffic calming measures into the design process, the department is authorized to deny any development permit application.
(b) Traffic calming measures incorporated in the construction phase of a development shall do so at no cost to the county. All capital construction costs associated with the traffic calming measures shall be the responsibility of the developer.
(c) A traffic calming tax district shall be created for the residential development upon final plat approval of the board of commissioners. The individual real property parcels within the development will be subject to the annual maintenance fee that shall be assessed by the county's tax assessor and collected by the county's tax commissioner, in compliance with the fee structure set by the board of commissioners.
(d) For a subdivision phase not completely built out and that did not go through the development process outlined in this article, a minimum of 30 percent of the total parcels must be occupied before a petition for traffic calming measures will be considered.
(Ord. No. 2025-250, § 1, 11-18-25)
